ai.subject: Pathology
ai.summary: Leukocyte alkaline phosphatase (LAP) is an enzyme activity measured in neutrophils. A low LAP score suggests a myeloproliferative disorder like CML, while a high score points to reactive causes such as infection.

sections.p: LAP is a cytoplasmic enzyme present in mature neutrophils. The LAP score quantifies its activity on a slide and helps differentiate leukocytosis causes.
b: Measured by staining peripheral blood smear and counting stained neutrophils (0‑4 per cell).
Score < 100 is considered low; > 200 is high.

t.b: Does the leukocytosis reflect a myeloproliferative neoplasm or a reactive process? Low score → CML or other clonal disorders; high score → infection, inflammation, leukemoid reaction.

sections.p: LAP itself is not staged, but its result guides staging of the underlying disease (e.g., chronic phase vs blast crisis in CML).
b: In CML, low LAP plus >100 × 10⁹/L leukocytes suggests chronic phase; rising blasts shift management.

sections.p: Low LAP is most often seen in clonal neutrophil proliferations; high LAP occurs in reactive conditions.
b: Low LAP: chronic myeloid leukemia, polycythemia vera, primary myelofibrosis.
High LAP: bacterial sepsis, severe tissue infection, leukemoid reaction, stress leukocytosis, sickle‑cell crisis.

sections.p: Patients present with signs of leukocytosis—fatigue, splenomegaly, weight loss for CML; fever, localized pain for infection.
b: CML: chronic fatigue, night sweats, massive splenomegaly, asymptomatic leukocytosis on routine labs.
Leukemoid reaction: high fever, source of infection, rapid rise in white count.

sections.p: Beyond the LAP score, confirm the underlying cause with targeted tests.
b: CBC with differential to quantify leukocytosis.
Peripheral smear for morphology.
BCR‑ABL PCR for CML confirmation.

t.b: What is the white cell count and maturation pattern? Marked left shift with high neutrophils supports reactive cause; full spectrum with basophilia points to CML.
Are there immature granulocytes, blasts, or dysplastic cells? Presence of many myelocytes and basophils favors CML.
Does the patient have the Philadelphia chromosome? Positive result confirms CML; negative makes reactive causes more likely.
Rely on cytogenetics (karyotype) or clinical picture; refer to a center with PCR capability when possible.

sections.p: Uncontrolled myeloproliferation can progress to blast crisis; infections can become septic.
b: Rapid rise in blasts (>20%) → imminent blast crisis.
Persistent fever, hypotension, organ dysfunction → sepsis.

sections.p: Treat the underlying disease; supportive care addresses cytopenias or infection.
b: CML: tyrosine‑kinase inhibitors (imatinib, dasatinib) because they target BCR‑ABL; avoid hydroxyurea long‑term due to resistance.
Reactive leukocytosis: antibiotics for bacterial infection, antimalarials for malaria, antiretrovirals for HIV‑related infections.
Monitor counts weekly until stable; watch for tumor lysis or hyperuricemia.

sections.p: Regular monitoring prevents progression and detects treatment failure.
b: CML: repeat BCR‑ABL PCR every 3 months; adjust therapy if no molecular response.
Infection: ensure source control, complete antimicrobial course, vaccinate where appropriate.

sections.p: Conditions that also cause high white counts but differ in LAP.
b: Leukemoid reaction (high LAP) vs CML (low LAP).
Polycythemia vera (low LAP) vs secondary erythrocytosis.

sections.p: LAP may be falsely normal in early CML or altered by certain drugs.
b: Steroid therapy can raise LAP, masking a low‑score disease.
Severe neutropenia limits ability to calculate a reliable LAP score.

whenToSeekHelp: Sudden onset of high fever with rapid white count rise (possible sepsis).
New splenomegaly and fatigue with rising leukocytes (possible CML progression).

faq.q: Why is LAP low in CML?
faq.a: Clonal neutrophils in CML are functionally immature and produce less alkaline phosphatase.

faq.q: Can a high LAP score rule out CML?
faq.a: A high score makes CML unlikely but does not exclude atypical variants; confirm with BCR‑ABL testing.

faq.q: What if I cannot get a LAP test?
faq.a: Rely on CBC morphology, clinical picture, and definitive molecular tests when available.

exam: Explain how the LAP score helps differentiate CML from a leukemoid reaction.
List the first‑line therapy for CML and why it is preferred over hydroxyurea.
Describe two clinical situations where a high LAP score is expected.
